questions.question: What trend occurs in atomic radius across a period?
questions.explanation: Atomic radius decreases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge pulling electrons closer to the nucleus.

questions.question: Which group of elements is known as alkali metals?
questions.explanation: Group 1 elements (Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr) are called alkali metals. They have one valence electron and are highly reactive.

questions.question: What is the name of Group 17 elements?
questions.explanation: Group 17 elements (F, Cl, Br, I, At) are called halogens. They have 7 valence electrons and are highly reactive nonmetals.

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity (4.0 on the Pauling scale). Electronegativity generally increases across a period.

questions.question: What is the trend in ionization energy down a group?
questions.explanation: Ionization energy decreases down a group because the valence electrons are farther from the nucleus and more shielded.

questions.question: Which group contains elements with a full valence shell?
questions.explanation: Group 18 elements (noble gases) have a full valence shell (8 electrons, except helium with 2) and are chemically inert.

questions.question: What is the modern periodic table organized by?
questions.explanation: The modern periodic table arranges elements by increasing atomic number (number of protons), not atomic mass.

questions.question: Which element is a liquid at room temperature and is in Group 17?
questions.explanation: Bromine (Br2) is the only nonmetal that is liquid at room temperature. It is a halogen in Group 17.
